SearchAliases: Zen he is now exactly me
Senses.Explanation: The surviving verse supplies the indispensable continuation: “I now go alone; everywhere I meet him. He is now exactly me; I am now not him. One must understand in this way to tally with thusness” (我今獨自往，處處得逢渠。渠今正是我，我今不是渠。應須與摩會，方得契如如). Later Caodong records explicitly say “the five ranks of lord and minister all issue from this” (五位君臣都從此出), turn each half into public questions, and criticize proposed uses: Yongjue comments “still separated by one mountain” after the first line, while Dahui Zonggao answers an unnamed monk’s use of the couplet by asking where the fault lies. The phrase’s Zen-specific identity is this named line in Dongshan’s water-reflection verse and its later deployment as a source line, interview question, and object of criticism. This entry does not resolve the pronouns beyond the verse’s wording.
